drhp.business: Jasch Industries Ltd manufactures PU/PVC coated fabrics - also known as synthetic or artificial leather - and polyurethane resin, organised into two business segments: PU Coated Fabrics & Allied Products and PVC Coated Fabrics & Allied Products. Its products are used mainly by the footwear industry (shoe uppers, linings, insoles, chappal and sandal straps), by the garment industry as lining material, by automobile makers as seat covers, and in furniture upholstery, purses, bags, luggage and sports goods. risks.note: Management states the company's products are mostly used in the footwear industry, so 'the fortunes of the company are invariably inter linked with those of footwear Industry' and any downward trend there may significantly impact the company. Diversification into automobile, general-purpose upholstery, sports goods and garment industries has reached only 40% of usage.

About 65% of raw materials (Dioctyl Phthalate, Dimethylformamide, PVC resin, man-made fabrics, pigments) are petroleum-based, so any increase in international crude-oil prices raises the cost of production. Price increases pass through to customers only with a lag of roughly three months and only if the whole market moves; the Board Report confirms the company 'has not been able to fully pass on the adverse impact of raw material and fuel prices to customers'. Management argues the contractual exposure itself is small because it holds no long-term contracts with suppliers or buyers, leaving less than 15 days' orders in hand at risk.
risks.risk: Petroleum-linked raw material cost / commodity risk

risks.note: The MD&A Outlook says the mandate of law to use only piped natural gas as fuel in factories located in the National Capital Region, which is nearly three times costlier than conventional fuel, together with erratic petroleum-based raw material prices, has 'significantly eroded Company's profits'. This is a structural, location-driven cost disadvantage for the Sonipat operations.
risks.risk: Regulated fuel cost - mandatory piped natural gas in the NCR

risks.note: The company faces significant competition from entities with longer operating histories, better brand recognition, greater financial resources, more advanced technology, better R&D and larger distribution networks, as well as from cheaper imports and smaller regional players competing on price and local trust. The MD&A separately notes the Indian synthetic leather industry has not achieved its potential because of tough competition from imported material from China, where very large units enjoy economies of scale and cheap local raw material and labour. Failure to compete could reduce market share and push prices down while raising marketing costs.
risks.risk: Competition, including cheaper imports from China

risks.note: Management explicitly names obsolescence of coated-fabrics technology as a threat, mitigated through in-house R&D since inception, foreign technical expertise and continuous upgradation - including an earlier technical collaboration with Duksung Company Ltd., Korea. The mitigation depends on sustained access to external technology rather than on scale R&D spend; the AR states no significant amount was spent on R&D and no technology was imported in the last three years.

Excessive exposure to a few large clients has the potential to adversely affect sales and profitability if clients fail or shift to other manufacturers. Management says its customers are currently fairly spread out across the country, with efforts underway to enlarge presence in eastern and southern markets - and the industry itself is concentrated in Northern and Western India.

Currency risk arises from downward fluctuation in foreign currency on the company's spending to import raw materials and consumables - a substantial and growing outgo relative to negligible export earnings. Transactions are on a current-account basis with no deferred foreign-exchange liabilities except amounts due on raw material imported on deferred-payment terms.
risks.risk: Currency fluctuation on a large import bill

risks.note: An increase in bank interest rates hits profitability because the increase cannot always be passed on to customers; management seeks to contain interest cost through efficient management of inventory and working capital resources.
